units.purpose: Describe error conditions and expected system responses in natural language.
units.content: Describe error conditions and expected system responses in natural language.
keywords: error-scenario
rejection
failure-case
exception

sections.title: Rejection of Unauthorized Todo Access
sections.content:
WHEN a user requests to view details, edit, toggle completion status, delete, restore, permanently delete, or view edit history for a todo, THEN the system SHALL reject the request if the todo is not owned by that user.

WHEN a user requests to view the edit history for a todo that is not owned by that user, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

WHEN a user requests any operation on a permanently deleted todo, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF the request references a todo that is not accessible to the authenticated user, THEN THE system SHALL reject the request.

sections.title: Failure-Case Validation for Todo Creation and Update Dates
sections.content:
WHEN a user attempts to create a todo, THEN the system SHALL reject the request if the required title value is missing.

WHEN a user attempts to create or update a todo, THEN the system SHALL reject the request if the due date is earlier than the start date (when both dates are provided).

WHEN a user attempts to update a todo’s title, THEN the system SHALL reject the update if the new title value is missing or empty.

WHEN a user attempts to update a todo’s start date and due date such that the due date becomes earlier than the start date, THEN the system SHALL reject the update.

WHEN a user provides an optional description as empty, THEN the system SHALL allow creation or update without a description.

WHEN a user provides an optional start date as empty, THEN the system SHALL allow creation or update without a start date.

WHEN a user provides an optional due date as empty, THEN the system SHALL allow creation or update without a due date.

sections.title: Exception Handling for Invalid Delete, Restore, and Permanent Delete State
sections.content:
WHEN a user deletes a todo, THEN the system SHALL move it into the trash so it no longer appears in the normal todo list.

WHEN a user restores a todo from the trash, THEN the system SHALL return it to the normal todo list.

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from the trash, THEN the system SHALL permanently remove that todo.

WHEN a todo is permanently deleted, THEN the system SHALL also permanently remove its edit history.

IF a user attempts to restore a todo that is not currently in the trash, THEN the system SHALL reject the restore request.

IF a user attempts to permanently delete a todo that is not currently in the trash, THEN the system SHALL reject the permanent deletion request.

IF a user attempts to delete, restore, or permanently delete a todo that is not owned by that user, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF a user attempts to permanently delete a todo that is already permanently deleted, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

sections.title: Failure-Case Handling for Completion Status Toggle
sections.content:
WHEN a user marks a todo as complete, THEN the system SHALL set the todo’s completion status to complete.

WHEN a user marks a todo as incomplete, THEN the system SHALL set the todo’s completion status to incomplete.

IF a user attempts to toggle completion status for a todo that is permanently deleted, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF a user attempts to toggle completion status for a todo that is not owned by that user, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF the request references a todo that the user cannot access, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

sections.title: Exception Handling for Edit History Recording and Display
sections.content:
WHEN a user edits a todo they own, THEN the system SHALL record an edit history entry for that todo.

WHEN the system records an edit history entry, THEN it SHALL include the time when the edit was made.

WHEN a user edits a todo and changes title, description, start date, and/or due date, THEN the system SHALL record only the attributes that were changed in the edit history entry.

WHEN a user edits a todo and a specific attribute among title, description, start date, and due date is not changed, THEN the system SHALL not display a “changed to” value for that attribute in the corresponding history entry.

WHEN a user views the edit history of a todo they own, THEN the system SHALL display the entries from most recent to oldest.

IF a user attempts to view edit history for a todo that is not owned by them, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF a user attempts to view edit history for a todo that is permanently deleted, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

sections.title: Rejection and Failure-Cases for Filtered and Sorted Todo List Browsing
sections.content:
WHEN a user requests to view their normal todo list, THEN the system SHALL include only todos owned by that user.

WHEN a user requests to view their trash list, THEN the system SHALL include only todos owned by that user.

WHEN a user filters the todo list by completion status, THEN the system SHALL return only todos matching the selected completion status for that user.

WHEN a user requests sorting by creation date, THEN the system SHALL apply newest-first or oldest-first ordering as selected.

WHEN a user requests sorting by start date, THEN the system SHALL place todos without a start date at the end of the ordered results.

WHEN a user requests sorting by due date, THEN the system SHALL place todos without a due date at the end of the ordered results.

IF a user requests to access a single todo that is not owned by them, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

IF a user requests to access a single todo that is permanently deleted, THEN the system SHALL reject the request.

files.summary: Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies
files.content:
**multiUserTodo — Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies**

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies

# Data Policies

Data ownership, privacy, retention, and recovery policies from a business perspective.

## Data Ownership and Privacy

Define who owns what data, who can access it, and privacy boundaries between users.

### Data Ownership Scope for User-Private Content

- THE system SHALL treat each user’s profile display name as data owned by that user.
- THE system SHALL treat each todo’s title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation date as data owned by the user who created the todo.
- THE system SHALL treat each todo’s edit history as data owned by the user who owns the todo.
- THE system SHALL ensure that ownership determines visibility and actions for todos and todo edit history.
- WHEN a user deletes their account, THE system SHALL permanently remove their todos from accessibility, including todos that are currently in trash.
- WHEN a user deletes their account, THE system SHALL permanently remove the edit history associated with that user’s todos from accessibility.

### Access Control Boundaries Between Users

- THE system SHALL require that, when viewing a list of todos, the system shows only todos owned by the currently signed-in user.
- THE system SHALL require that, when viewing a single todo, the system shows that todo only if it is owned by the currently signed-in user.
- THE system SHALL require that, when viewing a user’s trash list, the system shows only deleted todos owned by the currently signed-in user.
- THE system SHALL require that, when restoring a deleted todo from trash, the system allows restoration only for a todo owned by the currently signed-in user.
- THE system SHALL require that, when permanently deleting a todo from trash, the system permanently deletes only a todo owned by the currently signed-in user.
- THE system SHALL require that, when viewing edit history, the system shows only edit history entries for todos owned by the currently signed-in user.
- IF a user attempts to view, restore, edit, delete, or view history for a todo that is not owned by that user, THEN THE system SHALL deny access.

### Privacy Guarantees for User Profiles and Todos

- THE system SHALL keep the application private such that users cannot view or access other users’ profiles.
- THE system SHALL keep each user’s profile display name private from other users.
- THE system SHALL keep each user’s todos completely private from other users.
- THE system SHALL keep each user’s todo details private from other users, including the full description when a single todo is viewed.
- THE system SHALL keep each user’s deleted (soft-deleted) todos private so that other users cannot view or discover them via the trash view.
- THE system SHALL keep each user’s todo edit history private so that other users cannot view it.
- THE system SHALL ensure there is no way for a user to view, access, or share another user’s todos.

### Data Isolation Consistency Across All Todo States

- THE system SHALL enforce data isolation consistently across: normal todo viewing, single-todo viewing, trash viewing, restoring from trash, permanently deleting from trash, and viewing a todo’s edit history.
- WHILE a todo is in normal list visibility, THE system SHALL show it only to its owner.
- WHILE a todo is in trash, THE system SHALL show it only to its owner.
- WHEN a deleted todo is restored from trash, THE system SHALL return it to the owner’s normal todo list visibility.
- WHEN a todo is permanently deleted from trash, THE system SHALL remove the todo content and its edit history from accessibility for its owner as well.

## Data Retention and Recovery

Define what happens to deleted data, how long it is retained, and how users can recover it.

### Soft-Deleted Todo Retention Window and Expiration

WHEN a user deletes a todo, THE system SHALL move the todo into the user’s trash using soft-delete.
THE system SHALL retain soft-deleted todos for a defined retention window after they enter the trash.
WHEN the retention window ends for a specific soft-deleted todo, THE system SHALL remove that todo from the user’s trash.
WHEN a soft-deleted todo is removed due to the retention window ending, THEN the todo SHALL no longer be available for recovery.
THE system SHALL ensure that a removed-from-trash todo does not return to the trash or normal todo list unless the user performs a new create action for a new todo.

### Restoring a Todo from Trash

WHEN a user restores a todo from the trash, THE system SHALL return that todo to the user’s normal todo list.
WHEN restoration succeeds, THE system SHALL preserve the todo’s completion status as it was before deletion.
WHEN restoration succeeds, THE system SHALL preserve all details required for the user to view the todo after restoration, including its description, start date (if set), and due date (if set).
WHEN restoration succeeds, THE system SHALL preserve the todo’s full edit history so the user sees the same history after restoration.
IF a user attempts to restore a todo that is not present in their trash (for example, because it was removed after the retention window ended), THEN the restoration action SHALL be rejected.

### Permanent Deletion Finality for Trash Items and Edit History

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from the trash, THE system SHALL permanently remove the todo so it no longer appears in either the normal todo list or the trash list.
WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from the trash, THE system SHALL permanently remove the todo’s edit history.
IF a user attempts to permanently delete a todo that is not present in their trash, THEN the permanent-deletion action SHALL be rejected.
AFTER permanent deletion succeeds, THE system SHALL ensure the user cannot restore the deleted todo from trash.
AFTER permanent deletion succeeds, THE system SHALL ensure the user cannot view the deleted todo details or its edit history.

### `multi_user_todo_user_profiles`

Stores a user's private profile personalization details. The profile is
owned by exactly one user account, and other users must not be able to
view it.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key for the user profile record.
- `multi_user_todo_user_id`
  > Reference to the owning [multi_user_todo_user_profiles.id](#multi_user_todo_user_profiles) account.
  > Enforces that each user has at most one profile.
- `display_name`
  > User-facing display name presented in the app. This is a key profile
  > attribute used for personalization.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. When set, the profile is treated as deleted and is
  > no longer visible to the owning user.

### `multi_user_todo_todos`

Private task item owned by exactly one user and visible only to that user
across normal, completed, and trash states. Stores the todo's current
editable attributes plus timestamps for filtering, ordering, and soft
deletion visibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the todo item.
- `title`: Required human-readable title of the todo.
- `description`: Optional longer description for the todo; can be empty or null.
- `start_date`: Optional datetime indicating when the todo begins.
- `due_date`: Optional datetime deadline for the todo.

  > Lifecycle state controlling deletion flow and list visibility (e.g.,
  > normal vs trash).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of the todo record.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp of the todo record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft-delete timestamp. When non-null, the todo is considered deleted
  > (typically moved to trash) and excluded from normal lists.

### `multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries`

Immutable edit history entry for a specific todo.

Each row represents a single change event and stores both the previous
and new values for tracked todo attributes. This enables audit-style
inspection of how a user's todo changed over time, ordered most-recent to
oldest via edit_made_at and the created_at timestamps.

Entries are soft-deletable, and are permanently removed when the owning
todo is permanently removed per system retention rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key for the todo edit history entry.
- `multi_user_todo_todo_id`: Reference to [multi_user_todos.id](#multi_user_todos) for the todo that was edited.
- `multi_user_todo_owner_id`
  > Reference to the owning user of the edited todo, copied for efficient
  > ownership-scoped filtering.
- `edit_made_at`: Business time when the edit was made.
- `previous_title`: Previous todo title value before this edit.
- `new_title`: New todo title value after this edit.
- `previous_description`: Previous todo description value before this edit; null means it was empty.
- `new_description`: New todo description value after this edit; null means it is empty.
- `previous_start_date`: Previous todo start date before this edit; null means it was unset.
- `new_start_date`: New todo start date after this edit; null means it is unset.
- `previous_due_date`: Previous todo due date before this edit; null means it was unset.
- `new_due_date`: New todo due date after this edit; null means it is unset.
- `previous_is_complete`: Previous completion status before this edit.
- `new_is_complete`: New completion status after this edit.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for this history entry.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member’s profile display name for this private todo app.

This endpoint allows a signed-in member to change only their own UserProfile display_name stored in multi_user_todo_user_profiles.

Validation and privacy guarantees:
- The update must be scoped to the authenticated user’s own profile (multi_user_todo_user_id). The client must not be able to target another user’s profile.
- If the request would result in an empty display_name, the system rejects the update and keeps the existing value unchanged.
- If the authenticated user has no available (non-deleted) profile record, the update is rejected.

After the update is accepted, subsequent reads of the profile must reflect the newly saved display_name.
operations.name: updateProfile
operations.specification:
Implementation guidance for Realize Agent:

1. Authentication/context
- Require authenticated member context.
- Derive authenticatedUserId from the request context; do not accept any user identifier from the client for this operation.

2. Load and validate target profile
- Query multi_user_todo_user_profiles by multi_user_todo_user_id = authenticatedUserId.
- If no record exists or the record has deleted_at set (soft-deleted), reject as not found/unavailable for update.

3. Validate input
- Read display_name from the request body.
- Trim leading/trailing whitespace.
- Reject if trimmed display_name is empty (empty display name edit must be rejected and existing data preserved).

4. Persist update
- Update multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name with the validated value.
- Update multi_user_todo_user_profiles.updated_at to the current server timestamp.

5. Return response
- Return the updated multi_user_todo_user_profiles row as JSON.

6. Error handling
- For any validation failure, do not modify the database.
- For missing/unavailable profile, return an error indicating the profile cannot be updated.

responseBody.description: The updated profile record including the newly saved display_name.

requestBody.description: Profile update payload containing the new display_name for the authenticated user’s profile.

operations.description:

The profile is only available when it is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).

Implementation steps:
1) Require an authenticated member context (authenticated account id).
2) Validate profileId format (UUID) and return an error for invalid input.
3) Query multi_user_todo_user_profiles by id = profileId and deleted_at IS NULL.
4) If no row matches, return a not-found/unavailable response (treated as unavailable).
5) Ownership enforcement: verify the row’s multi_user_todo_user_id equals the authenticated user id.
   - If it does not match, deny access (do not reveal whether the profile exists for another user).
6) Map fields to response:
   - id
   - multi_user_todo_user_id (if present in the DTO; otherwise omit in mapping layer)
   - display_name
   - created_at
   - updated_at
7) Do not join or return any todo or edit history data; profile operations are independent of todo ownership visibility.

Error handling:
- Invalid UUID => 400-like validation error.
- Not found or soft-deleted => 404-like not found.
- Ownership mismatch => 403-like forbidden/access denied.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user’s profile display name.

This endpoint allows a signed-in member to change only their own private profile personalization data: the profile display name.

Privacy and authorization are enforced with a self-only boundary: the request must apply to the profile owned by the authenticated user, and any attempt to target a different profile must be denied. Reading or updating another user’s profile is not allowed.

Validation rejects empty display names: if the submitted display name is empty after trimming, the system rejects the update and keeps the existing display name unchanged.

The update must not affect todo data visibility rules; it only changes the authenticated user’s user profile record.
operations.name: put
operations.specification:
Implement PUT /profile as an ownership-scoped update on multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name.

Service logic:
1) Authentication requirement:
   - Require the caller to be an authenticated member.
   - Resolve the authenticated user's id from the session context as the owner scope.
2) Target row selection:
   - Find the single multi_user_todo_user_profiles row where multi_user_todo_user_id equals the authenticated user id.
   - The profile must be visible: treat deleted rows (deleted_at != null) as not visible. If no visible row exists, deny/not-found per service conventions.
3) Request validation:
   - Accept a payload containing the new display name.
   - Trim whitespace and ensure display_name is not empty.
   - If display_name becomes empty, reject the update without writing changes.
4) Database update:
   - Update multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name.
   - Update multi_user_todo_user_profiles.updated_at.
   - Do not modify deleted_at.
5) Response:
   - Return the updated multi_user_todo_user_profiles entity.

Error handling:
- Unauthenticated: deny.
- Missing/soft-deleted profile for the authenticated user: deny/not-found.
- Validation failure (empty display name after trim): return a validation error and do not update.

Edge cases:
- Concurrent requests: apply standard last-write-wins behavior unless the underlying stack provides optimistic locking.

responseBody.description: The updated authenticated user's profile including the newly saved display name.

requestBody.description: Update payload containing the new non-empty display name for the authenticated user’s profile.

This endpoint returns the current authenticated user’s private profile, including the display name used for personalization.

Authorization and privacy:
- Only an authenticated member can access this endpoint.
- The system must not allow retrieving any other user’s profile; if the request context does not match the profile being read, access must be denied.

Unavailable cases:

1) Require member authentication (reject unauthenticated requests).
2) Resolve the authenticated user's id from the session context.
3) Query multi_user_todo_user_profiles for exactly one row where multi_user_todo_user_id = authenticated user id.
4) If no row exists, return a profile-not-found/unavailable error.
5) If deleted_at is set (non-null), treat the profile as unavailable and return the same profile-not-found/unavailable error.
6) Map the row to the response DTO, including at minimum: id and display_name.

DB mapping reference:

- Columns used: id (uuid), multi_user_todo_user_id (uuid), display_name (string), deleted_at (timestamptz nullable).

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member’s private profile display name.

This operation lets a signed-in member change only their own profile display name (the key user-facing personalization attribute). The system enforces a self-only boundary: a member cannot view or update another user’s profile, and an unauthorized or unauthenticated request must be rejected with no changes applied.

Business validation is applied to the provided display name: if the request submits an empty or otherwise invalid display name, the system rejects the update and keeps the previously saved value unchanged.

For concurrency and rapid successive updates, the system ensures the member’s profile ends in a consistent state (a valid update is applied; an invalid update is rejected without overwriting a more recent valid value).
operations.name: patch
operations.specification:
Implement PATCH /profile as an authenticated, user-scoped update against multi_user_todo_user_profiles.

1) Authentication & scope resolution
- Require an authenticated member.
- Resolve the profile row using the authenticated user identity mapped to multi_user_todo_user_profiles.multi_user_todo_user_id (do not accept or trust any user id from the request body).

2) Request validation
- Parse request body and require display_name to be present.
- Apply the profile display name business validation rules (reject missing or invalid display_name).
- If validation fails, do not modify the stored display_name.

3) Visibility handling
- Treat the profile as not visible when multi_user_todo_user_profiles.deleted_at is non-null.
- If no visible profile exists for the authenticated user, reject with an error indicating the profile cannot be updated.

4) Atomic update / race consistency
- Perform the update in a way that guarantees consistency under simultaneous update attempts (e.g., transaction with proper isolation or optimistic concurrency), so an invalid request never partially applies and a valid request results in a consistent final display_name.

5) Update rules
- Update only multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name and updated_at.
- Do not change multi_user_todo_user_profiles.multi_user_todo_user_id.

6) Response
- On success, return the updated multi_user_todo_user_profiles record.

7) Error handling
- Authorization/authentication failures: deny without changing any data.
- Validation failures: reject without changing display_name.
- Profile not visible for the authenticated user: reject with an appropriate error.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo for the authenticated member by its identifier.

This operation returns the requested todo entity identified by `todoId`.

Privacy isolation is enforced: if the todo does not belong to the authenticated member, the request must be rejected and the todo data must not be returned.

Permanently removed todos are treated as non-retrievable: when the requested todo is not accessible through normal or trash views, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1) Authenticate the request as a member.
2) Parse `todoId` as UUID.
3) Query `multi_user_todo_todos` for a row where `id = todoId`.
4) Enforce ownership isolation by ensuring the todo belongs to the authenticated member.
   - Implement by scoping the todo lookup to the authenticated owner (e.g., join or filter using an owner identifier available in the session/context and the todo’s persisted owner scope).
5) Enforce deletion visibility policy for “permanently deleted / non-retrievable” todos.
   - If the todo is permanently removed or otherwise not accessible through normal/trash views, reject the request.
6) Map the todo row to the response DTO.
7) If the response DTO includes edit history data, load related `multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries` for `multi_user_todo_todo_id = todoId`, ordered by `edit_made_at` descending (most recent first), and map to the DTO.

Error handling:
- Reject when no accessible todo is found (including not-owned or permanently deleted cases). Do not reveal whether the id exists for other users.

operations.description:
Search and list the authenticated member’s todos.

This operation returns a paginated list of todo summaries visible only to the signed-in member who owns them.

The filtering supports completion status and time-based constraints using the todo’s current attributes, and sorting/pagination for efficient browsing.

Privacy and error handling:
- All queries must be scoped to the authenticated owner.
- If the request targets or implies a todo outside the authenticated member’s ownership, the system must deny the action without leaking other users’ todo content or identifiers.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement PATCH /todos as a member-scoped list/search over multi_user_todo_todos.

1) Authentication/identity
- Require an authenticated member in the request context.

2) Base query and privacy isolation
- Start from multi_user_todos and restrict results to todos owned by the authenticated member.
- Enforce privacy isolation at the query layer so only owned rows are eligible for filtering and sorting.

3) Visibility and lifecycle
- Apply lifecycle/deletion visibility according to request filters.
- Use multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at and multi_user_todo_todos.lifecycle_state to determine which rows are eligible for the requested list mode (normal vs trash vs other lifecycle_state values as defined by the domain).

4) Filtering
- Apply optional filters from the request (e.g., completion status using multi_user_todo_todos.is_complete, date ranges using created_at/start_date/due_date, and keyword matching against multi_user_todo_todos.title and multi_user_todo_todos.description if provided).
- Validate that provided date ranges are logically ordered (e.g., from <= to). Reject invalid ranges as validation errors.

5) Sorting
- Apply requested sorting with an allowlist of sortable fields; default to multi_user_todo_todos.created_at descending.

6) Pagination
- Apply pagination parameters from the request and return a paginated result.

7) Mapping
- Map each selected todo row to the corresponding todo summary DTO (exclude heavy/history fields).

8) Errors
- Return validation errors for invalid filters/sort keys.
- Do not return any information about non-owned todos; never vary error messages in a way that could confirm the existence of other users’ todos.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summary records matching the provided search criteria, scoped to the authenticated member.

operations.description:
Create a new todo owned by the requesting member.

This endpoint allows a member to create a private task item. The created todo is isolated to the authenticated user and cannot be accessed by other members.

Validation and defaults: a title is required; if the title is missing, the request is rejected and no todo is created. When creation succeeds, the todo is stored as incomplete by default, regardless of any completion-related values the client might provide.

Error handling: if the request fails validation (e.g., missing title) or violates domain invariants (e.g., a creation flow that would result in an initially-completed todo), the system rejects the request without creating a database record.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1) Authenticate the caller as a member and derive the todo owner from the authenticated identity (never accept any owner/user identifier from the client).
2) Parse JSON body into the component DTO type MultiUserTodoTodo.ICreate.
3) Validate required fields:
   - Reject if title is missing or empty.
4) Enforce the creation default:
   - Persist the todo with is_complete=false (incomplete). If the parsed DTO/state indicates a completed initial state, reject the creation.
5) Map DTO fields to multi_user_todo_todos columns:
   - title -> title
   - description -> description (nullable)
   - start_date -> start_date (nullable)
   - due_date -> due_date (nullable)
   - lifecycle_state -> set to the service’s default “normal list visibility” state used for normal vs trash filtering (do not rely on deleted_at alone).
   - deleted_at -> must be null on creation
   - created_at / updated_at -> set by persistence/database layer
6) Privacy isolation enforcement:
   - Ensure any subsequent operations use owner scoping; this create endpoint must never write or return data for any other user.
7) Transactionality:
   - Perform validation before insert; if validation fails, do not create any row.
8) Return the created todo entity as stored.

responseBody.description: The created todo entity owned by the requesting member, including its id, scheduling fields, and current lifecycle/completion state.

requestBody.description: Todo creation payload. Title is required; description and scheduling dates are optional. Newly created todos are always stored as incomplete by default.

operations.description:
Updates a member-owned todo by its ID.

This endpoint lets the authenticated member modify the todo’s editable attributes such as title, optional description, optional start date, optional due date, and its completion status.

Privacy isolation is enforced: the system only allows updates to todos owned by the requesting member, and it rejects requests targeting permanently deleted or otherwise inaccessible todos.

For audit traceability, the system records a todo edit history entry capturing previous and new values for each tracked attribute at the time of the edit.
operations.name: updateTodo
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1. Authenticate the caller as a member.
2. Validate todoId is a UUID.
3. Load the todo row by id = {todoId} with an ownership constraint matching the authenticated member (e.g., join/filter by multi_user_todo_todos owner if available in your auth context; if ownership is not directly stored on the todos table, resolve owner via the request context and ensure the todo belongs to that owner).
4. If no accessible todo exists for the authenticated member, reject the request (do not reveal whether the todo exists).
5. Reject the request if the targeted todo is permanently deleted/inaccessible per lifecycle/deletion rules (e.g., if it is not eligible for editing due to its lifecycle_state/deleted_at status).
6. Validate input according to business rules for todos:
   - title is required
   - description can be empty or null (as represented by the request DTO)
   - start_date and due_date may be unset/null
7. Compute previous values from the loaded todo row for all tracked fields.
8. Apply updates to multi_user_todo_todos:
   - title
   - description
   - start_date
   - due_date
   - is_complete
   - updated_at = now
9. Insert a new multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries row capturing:
   - multi_user_todo_todo_id = todo.id
   - multi_user_todo_owner_id = todo owner id (from the authenticated member)
   - edit_made_at = now
   - previous_title/new_title
   - previous_description/new_description
   - previous_start_date/new_start_date (nullable)
   - previous_due_date/new_due_date (nullable)
   - previous_is_complete/new_is_complete
   - created_at = now
   - updated_at = now
   - deleted_at = null (active history entry)
10. Commit as a single transaction.

Error handling:
- Invalid UUID or invalid request DTO values: return validation errors.
- Unauthorized/non-owner todo access: reject.
- Permanently deleted/inaccessible todo: reject.

Edge cases:
- If optional fields are provided as empty/unset in the request DTO, write null/unset into the todo fields and store null in history entry where the previous/new values are unset.

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity after successfully applying the member’s changes, including current completion status and timestamps.

parameters.description: Identifier of the todo to update (global scope UUID).
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the todo. Ownership context is provided by the authenticated member and todoId path parameter.

operations.description:
Delete a todo owned by the authenticated member.

This operation moves the member-owned todo into the member’s trash lifecycle. After deletion, the todo is hidden from the member’s normal todo list and appears in the member’s trash list.

Privacy and ownership enforcement: if the todo is not owned by the currently authenticated member, the system rejects the request.

If the referenced todo is already permanently removed or otherwise inaccessible, the system rejects the request without modifying data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement as a member-scoped erase operation.

1) Authenticate and scope
- Require authenticated member access.
- Treat `todoId` as referencing a single row in `multi_user_todo_todos`.
- Enforce ownership isolation by ensuring the fetched todo is owned by the authenticated member (use the service’s existing ownership-scoping strategy). If no accessible row exists, reject.

2) Validate lifecycle accessibility
- If the todo is not accessible to the authenticated member (including permanently removed/unretrievable states), reject.

3) Soft delete (move to trash)
- In a transaction, update `multi_user_todo_todos` for the matched todo:
  - Set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp.
  - Update `lifecycle_state` to the system’s canonical value representing the trash lifecycle state.
  - Update `updated_at` to the current timestamp.

4) Response
- On success, return HTTP 204 with no JSON body.

5) Error handling
- Return an authorization/ownership error when the todo is not owned by the authenticated member.
- Return not-found/inaccessible-style errors when the todo cannot be accessed.
- Ensure the transaction prevents partial outcomes (either all updates happen or none).

parameters.description: UUID of the todo to delete. The todo must be owned by the authenticated member; otherwise the request is rejected (ownership isolation).
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve an authenticated owner’s edit history entries for a specific todo.

This operation returns the complete, audit-style change history for a single todo item that belongs to the authenticated user.

Edit history entries are presented from most recent to oldest so the user can trace how the todo changed over time.

Access is strictly scoped: if the requested todo is not owned by the authenticated user (or is otherwise inaccessible), the system rejects the request.

If the todo has never been edited since it was created, the system returns an empty edit-history page rather than treating it as an error.
operations.name: editHistoryEntries
operations.specification:
1) Authenticate the caller and obtain authenticatedUserId.
2) Validate path parameter todoId format (UUID) if applicable.
3) Ownership and accessibility check (privacy isolation):
   - Query multi_user_todo_todos for id = {todoId} and (implicit ownership) ensure multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries ownership match will be applied.
   - For the edit history query itself, enforce both constraints:
     - multi_user_todo_todo_id = {todoId}
     - multi_user_todo_owner_id = authenticatedUserId
   - If the todo referenced by {todoId} is not owned by the authenticated user, reject the request.
4) Fetch paginated edit history entries:
   - Filter multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries with the two ownership constraints above.
   - Order results by edit_made_at DESC.
   - Apply pagination from request body (limit/offset or cursor depending on IRequest DTO design).
5) Return a paginated response:
   - If no entries exist for the todo, return an empty page.
6) Error handling:
   - Reject unauthorized/non-owned todo access.
   - Do not create, update, or delete any data in this operation.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of the requested todo’s edit history entries for the authenticated owner, ordered from most recent to oldest.

parameters.description: Identifier of the todo whose edit history entries are requested (must be UUID).
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters (and any supported list/browsing criteria) for viewing the todo’s edit history entries.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific todo edit history entry for the requesting member.

This endpoint returns the immutable audit-style record representing one edit event of a todo. Access is strictly scoped to the authenticated member’s own todo data.

Privacy and access enforcement:
- The requested todo must be owned by the requesting member.
- The requested edit history entry must belong to the referenced todo.
- If either ownership/linkage check fails, the system must reject the request.

Trash visibility:
- The edit history remains available to the owner even when the todo is currently in trash.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1) Validate path parameters:
   - todoId must be a UUID.
   - todoEditHistoryEntryId must be a UUID.

2) Ownership isolation (todo):
   - Query multi_user_todos by id = todoId AND multi_user_todos.multi_user_owner_id scope via the authenticated member context.
   - If the todo is not found under the requesting member’s ownership, reject (ownership/access rejection).

3) Linkage validation (edit history entry):
   - Query multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries where id = todoEditHistoryEntryId AND multi_user_todo_todo_id = todoId.
   - If not found, reject (not-found/ownership-rejection as per error model).

4) Response:
   - Map the edit history row fields to the response DTO, including:
     - id
     - multi_user_todo_todo_id
     - multi_user_todo_owner_id
     - edit_made_at
     - previous_title, new_title
     - previous_description, new_description
     - previous_start_date, new_start_date
     - previous_due_date, new_due_date
     - previous_is_complete, new_is_complete
     - created_at, updated_at
     - deleted_at (may be null)

5) Edge cases:
   - Do not block access when multi_user_todos.deleted_at is non-null; edit history must still be returned for the owning member.
   - Never return an edit history entry that fails the todoId linkage check.

responseBody.description: The requested todo edit history entry, including the previous and new values recorded for that edit event.

parameters.description: UUID of the todo to which the edit history entry belongs. The system must verify this todo is owned by the requesting member.
parameters.name: todoId

parameters.description: UUID of the edit history entry to retrieve. The system must ensure this entry belongs to the referenced todoId.
parameters.name: todoEditHistoryEntryId

operations.description:
Return an authenticated member’s todo dashboard summary (normal vs trash).

This endpoint provides a single aggregated overview so the client can render counts and quick status indicators without browsing full todo lists.

Privacy and visibility are enforced:
- The system only considers todos owned by the authenticated member.
- Normal vs trash separation is respected using deleted_at-based visibility (normal excludes deleted todos; trash includes deleted-but-not-permanently-removed todos).
- The operation does not allow mixing normal and trashed results; it only returns the pre-separated aggregates.

Error handling:
- If the authenticated user context is missing/invalid, access fails via the existing authentication layer.
- If no todos exist in a bucket, counts are returned as 0.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:
1) Authenticate request as member; derive authenticatedMemberId from auth context.
2) Query multi_user_todo_todos for records scoped to the authenticated owner.
   - Use multi_user_todos.deleted_at to separate buckets:
     - Normal bucket: deleted_at IS NULL.
     - Trash bucket: deleted_at IS NOT NULL.
   - Apply lifecycle_state constraints consistently if the service-layer defines additional trash/visibility semantics for lifecycle_state; otherwise keep visibility aligned with deleted_at rules.
3) Compute aggregates for each bucket using only the fields available in the schema:
   - totalCount: COUNT(*).
   - completeCount: COUNT WHERE is_complete = true.
   - incompleteCount: COUNT WHERE is_complete = false.
   - startDateSetCount: COUNT WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL.
   - dueDateSetCount: COUNT WHERE due_date IS NOT NULL.
   - createdAtNewestAt/OldestAt (if supported by the DTO): derive from created_at.
4) Never expose individual todo rows or any content beyond the summary DTO.
5) Return a single JSON object matching IMultiUserTodoTodoSummary.

Edge cases:
- No rows in a bucket: return counts as 0.
- Ensure privacy isolation: do not accept any client-provided owner identifiers; always use authenticatedMemberId for scoping.

responseBody.description: Aggregated dashboard summary for normal vs trash todos owned by the authenticated member.

operations.description:
Move multiple authenticated-member todos into the user's trash in one request.

This operation bulk-transitions the specified todos that belong to the authenticated member from the normal (not deleted) view into the trash view.

Privacy isolation is enforced: if the request includes any todo not owned by the authenticated member, the system denies the action and returns no updates (no partial outcomes).

Soft-delete behavior is implemented by setting the todo soft-delete timestamp (deleted_at) and updating the todo lifecycle_state so that the moved todos no longer appear in the normal todo list and become visible only in the trash list.

Error handling returns clear client-facing errors for invalid payloads and ownership mismatches, and uses transactional updates to guarantee all-or-nothing behavior.
operations.name: bulkMoveToTrash
operations.specification:
Authorization/actor gating:
- Allow only authenticated member access. Deny guest.

Request validation:
- Validate that the request body contains an array of todo ids.
- Reject malformed payloads with 400.
- If the array is empty, reject with 400 (or treat as no-op if the downstream DTO contract specifies; default to 400).

Ownership & privacy isolation (all-or-nothing):
- Using the authenticated member's user id from the session, load todos whose id is in the provided list AND (multi_user_todos.multi_user_todo_owner_id / ownership-scoped filter is satisfied).
- Verify that the number of found todos equals the number of provided ids.
- If any id is missing or belongs to a different owner, abort with an authorization/ownership error and perform zero updates.

List separation constraint:
- This endpoint must transition from normal view to trash; only update todos that are currently not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) and match the normal-view invariant as defined by lifecycle_state/deleted_at.
- If the underlying domain defines specific lifecycle_state values for trash/normal, set lifecycle_state to the trash/deleted value.

Persistence (transaction):
- Within a single DB transaction, update all validated todos:
  - set deleted_at = now()
  - set lifecycle_state = trash/deleted lifecycle_state value
  - update updated_at = now()
- Ensure no partial updates: if any update fails, roll back.

Response:
- Return a bulk result summary DTO that includes at least movedCount.
- Optionally include updated todo summaries if supported by IMultiUserTodoTodo.IBulkMoveToTrashResult.

Error mapping:
- 400: validation failures.
- 403/404: ownership mismatch or non-existent ids according to the service's established mapping; never return partial results.
- 500: unexpected persistence failures.

responseBody.description: Bulk result indicating how many todos were moved from the normal list into the user's trash.

requestBody.description: Bulk request containing the todo ids to move from the authenticated member's normal list into trash.

operations.description:
Restore multiple trashed todos back to the normal todo list for the authenticated member in a single request.

This operation lets a signed-in member select multiple todo items currently in their trash and restore them so they appear in the normal (non-deleted) todo list.

Privacy isolation is enforced: a member can only restore their own todos, and any attempt to restore another member’s todo is rejected.

The operation is trash-only: every requested todo must currently be eligible for restore (i.e., it belongs to the member and is in trash). If any requested todo is not eligible (not owned by the member and/or not in the member’s trash), the system fails the entire request and does not modify any todos.

On success, the restore results correspond one-to-one with the requested todo IDs (no duplicate normal todo entries).
operations.name: bulkRestoreFromTrash
operations.specification:
Implement the endpoint as an all-or-nothing bulk restore.

1) Identify request scope and ownership
- Obtain the authenticated member’s user id from session/context.
- For each todoId in the request, only consider the todo row that matches:
  - multi_user_todos.id = todoId
  - multi_user_todos.multi_user_todo_owner_id scope via existing ownership enforcement strategy (use the service’s member scoping rules; when querying, restrict to todos owned by the authenticated member).

2) Validate trash eligibility (no restore unless in trash)
- A todo is eligible for restore only when:
  - multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at is non-null (the record is currently soft-deleted / in trash)
  - lifecycle_state is consistent with the domain’s trash state (use the domain state flow to set lifecycle_state to the appropriate active/normal value).
- If any requested todoId is not owned by the member or is not currently eligible for restore, fail the request.
- On failure: perform no updates at all.

3) All-or-nothing transaction
- Wrap validation and updates in a single database transaction.
- If any todo fails validation, roll back so that no todo is restored.

4) Restore update by existing ID (avoid duplicates)
- For each eligible todo record:
  - Set multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at = null.
  - Update multi_user_todo_todos.lifecycle_state to the normal/active lifecycle_state per the domain state flow.
  - Do not create new todo rows; only update the matched existing records by ID.

5) Handle duplicate IDs in input
- De-duplicate todoIds at the service layer to prevent double-processing within the transaction.

6) Response building
- Return a per-todoId result summary reflecting success/failure.
- When the operation fails due to any ineligible todo, return an error outcome consistent with the service error model and ensure no records were modified.

responseBody.description: Bulk restore results, including per-todoId status so the client can reflect which requested todos were restored.

requestBody.description: Bulk restore request containing the list of todo IDs to restore from the authenticated member’s trash.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes multiple of the authenticated member’s todos, including todos currently in trash.

This endpoint removes the specified todo records permanently so they do longer appear in either the normal todo list or the trash list for the requesting member.

The deletion also permanently removes the associated todo edit history entries, ensuring the member cannot retrieve any previous changes for deleted todos.

Privacy isolation is enforced: a member can only permanently delete their own todos. If the request contains any todo ID that is not owned by the authenticated member, the system must avoid partial outcomes and must not delete anything.

Error handling covers request validation (e.g., empty or invalid IDs), ownership/consistency checks, and unexpected server failures.
operations.name: bulkPermanentDelete
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1) Authenticate the request to get the authenticated member owner identity (ownerId).

2) Validate request body:
- Require a non-empty list of todo IDs.
- De-duplicate todo IDs at the service layer.
- Reject invalid UUID strings according to the request DTO validation.

3) Ownership and consistency check (anti-partial behavior):
- In a transaction, query multi_user_todo_todos for todos where id IN todoIds and multi_user_todo_owner_id corresponds to the authenticated owner identity (enforce membership privacy).
- If the count of matched todos is not equal to the count of unique requested IDs, abort the transaction and return an ownership/consistency error without performing any deletion.

4) Permanent deletion:
- Permanently delete the selected multi_user_todos rows.
- Ensure associated edit history entries are permanently removed as well. Prefer database-level cascade if configured; otherwise explicitly delete from multi_user_todo_todo_edit_history_entries where multi_user_todo_todo_id IN selectedTodoIds.

5) Edge cases:
- Todos may be in normal state or trash (deleted_at non-null or lifecycle_state indicates trash). Both must be permanently removed.
- If deletion fails for any reason, roll back to guarantee no partial outcomes.

6) Response:
- Return a summary of how many todos were deleted and the list/count of deleted IDs consistent with the DTO schema.

responseBody.description: Deletion result summary indicating how many todos were permanently deleted for the requesting member.

requestBody.description: Bulk permanent deletion request containing the todo IDs to remove permanently for the authenticated member.

operations.description:
Toggle completion status (complete ⇄ incomplete) for multiple owned todos in a single request.

This operation lets a member select several of their own todos and switch each todo’s completion status between complete and incomplete.

Privacy isolation is enforced strictly: the server only applies changes to todos owned by the authenticated member, and rejects the request if any referenced todo is not accessible to that member. When rejected, no todo completion changes are applied.

New todos start as incomplete by default; this endpoint only toggles the existing completion state and never attempts to create new todos.
operations.name: bulkToggleCompletion
operations.specification:
Implement a single atomic transaction that toggles completion status for all provided todo ids.

1) Authentication/ownership scope
- Require an authenticated member.
- Determine the authenticated member’s user id to scope all todo access (only allow updates where todo ownership matches the authenticated user).

2) Input validation
- Accept request body of type IMultiUserTodoBulkToggleCompletion.IRequest.
- Validate the todo id collection is present and contains at least one id.

3) Ownership and accessibility enforcement (all-or-nothing)
- Query multi_user_todo_todos for all requested ids filtered to the authenticated owner.
- Also ensure the requested todos are accessible for standard operations by honoring lifecycle/deletion visibility rules as implemented by the service layer:
  - Do not allow updates for todos that are permanently deleted/inaccessible.
  - Use lifecycle_state and/or deleted_at visibility semantics consistent with the existing service.
- Compare requested ids vs resolved/eligible ids.
  - If any id is missing from the eligible set, reject the entire operation and do not update any rows.

4) Toggle logic
- For each eligible todo, compute next_is_complete = NOT is_complete.
- Update multi_user_todos.is_complete to next_is_complete and set multi_user_todos.updated_at.

5) Transactionality
- Perform all updates within one DB transaction.
- If any validation/authorization/access check fails, rollback so completion status remains unchanged for all todos.

6) Response
- Return updated todo summaries for the eligible/updated set using the response DTO type.
- Use a deterministic ordering (e.g., ascending by todo id) if the DTO does not specify an order.

7) Error handling
- Reject with an authorization/access error if the request references any todo not owned by the authenticated member.
- Reject with a validation error for malformed payloads (e.g., empty todo id list).

responseBody.description: Updated completion-state results for the specified owned todos, suitable for refreshing client list/detail UI.

requestBody.description: Bulk toggle request specifying which todo ids the authenticated member wants to toggle between complete and incomplete.

operations.description:
Search the authenticated member’s todos with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This operation returns a paginated list of todo items belonging to the requesting authenticated user only. It supports browsing normal vs trash items (via lifecycle state / deletion visibility), filtering by completion status, and ordering by creation date, start date, or due date.

Privacy isolation is enforced: if the request would target todos not owned by the authenticated member, the system must deny access by only returning items that are owned by that member. The result set must exclude permanently deleted todos.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only search over multi_user_todo_todos scoped to the authenticated member.

1) Authorization & privacy isolation
- Resolve the authenticated user identity (member) and use it as the ownership scope.
- All queries must be constrained to todos owned by the requesting user.
- Ensure permanently deleted todos are excluded from results.

2) Inputs (from IMultiUserTodo.IRequest)
- Apply completion filtering when provided (use multi_user_todo_todos.is_complete).
- Apply lifecycle browsing selection when provided (use multi_user_todo_todos.lifecycle_state and/or multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at visibility semantics as defined by the domain).
- Apply text search on title and description when provided (use trigram-backed searching on multi_user_todo_todos.title and multi_user_todo_todos.description if a search text field is present).

3) Sorting rules
- Sort by created_at when requested; support newest-first or oldest-first.
- When sorting by start_date, place todos with start_date IS NULL at the end of the ordered results.
- When sorting by due_date, place todos with due_date IS NULL at the end of the ordered results.
- Apply a deterministic secondary order (e.g., id or created_at) to keep pagination stable.

4) Pagination
- Apply pagination parameters exactly as defined by the request DTO.
- Do not change the semantics of pagination during filtering/sorting.

5) Output mapping
- Map each matching todo row into IMultiUserTodoTodo.ISummary items (or the list-summary DTO required by the interface contract for this operation).
- Include only the fields required by the summary DTO.

6) Validation & error handling
- If filter/sort/pagination values are invalid per DTO validation, return a validation error.
- If ownership scope cannot be satisfied for the authenticated user, return an empty result set (do not leak existence of other users’ todos).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries matching the provided filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for the authenticated member.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including filtering by completion and lifecycle/visibility, optional text matching for title/description, sorting selection, and pagination.

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors; no access to private user profile or todo data.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated user who can manage their own account, private profile, and their own todos including trash and edit history.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

display_name.description:
New profile display name for the authenticated member.

The server trims whitespace and rejects updates where the trimmed value is empty. When the update succeeds, this display name is saved to the authenticated member’s own private profile record and will be returned by subsequent profile reads.
display_name.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name.

Processing steps:
1) Read display_name from the request body.
2) Trim leading/trailing whitespace.
3) If trimmed display_name is empty, reject the request and do not update the database.
4) Persist the trimmed value to multi_user_todo_user_profiles.display_name for the profile row resolved from the authenticated member’s identity.
5) Update multi_user_todo_user_profiles.updated_at to the current server timestamp as part of a successful update.

IMultiUserTodoUserProfile.IUpdate.description:
Update payload used by a signed-in member to change their own private profile personalization.

The member submits a single value, display_name. The server scopes the update to the authenticated member’s profile and validates that the provided display_name is not empty after trimming whitespace. On success, the new display_name is saved and reflected in subsequent profile reads. Server-managed fields (identifiers, audit timestamps, and soft-delete status) are never modified by this request.
IMultiUserTodoUserProfile.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
This DTO represents the authenticated member’s request payload for updating only their own private UserProfile display name.

Implementation rules
- Server derives the target profile row by resolving the authenticated member’s identity to multi_user_todo_user_profiles.multi_user_todo_user_id.
- The client supplies only display_name; the server must ignore any attempt to change other profile fields.
- Input validation: trim leading/trailing whitespace from display_name; reject if the trimmed value is empty.

Persistence rules

IMultiUserTodoTodo.IBulkRestoreFromTrash.x-autobe-specification:
Implements an all-or-nothing bulk restore operation for the authenticated member.

Input semantics:
- todoIds is the client-provided list of candidate todo identifiers (UUID strings).

Service/data access rules:
1) De-duplicate todoIds at the service layer to avoid double-processing within the same transaction.
2) Ownership scoping: only consider rows in multi_user_todos that belong to the authenticated member (enforced via the service’s existing member ownership scoping strategy).
3) Trash-only eligibility:
   - The todo row must be currently soft-deleted: multi_user_todos.deleted_at must be non-null.
   - The todo row’s multi_user_todos.lifecycle_state must be compatible with being restored from trash back to the domain’s normal/active lifecycle_state (use the domain state flow).
4) All-or-nothing transaction:
   - Validate eligibility for every provided todoId.
   - If any todoId is ineligible (wrong owner and/or not in trash and/or lifecycle_state incompatible), the entire request must fail and no rows are updated.
5) Restore update for eligible todos (by existing id):
   - Set multi_user_todos.deleted_at = null.
   - Update multi_user_todos.lifecycle_state to the domain’s normal/active lifecycle_state.
   - Do not create new todo rows.

Output handling:
- This request DTO only carries identifiers. Per-todo outcome details are returned by the endpoint’s result DTO.

Search and filtering controls for an authenticated member’s todo list.

This request body is sent to PATCH /multiUserTodo/member/todos. It lets the client optionally:
- choose which visibility scope to browse (normal vs trash),
- filter by completion state,
- optionally search by keyword within title/description,
- optionally constrain time ranges (created/start/due),
- choose sorting (field + direction), and
- request a specific page of results.

The server must enforce ownership isolation by applying all criteria only to todos owned by the authenticated member.
IMultiUserTodoTodo.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Direct request mapping for PATCH /multiUserTodo/member/todos.

Purpose
- Provide an authenticated member with optional controls to filter, sort, and paginate the member’s visible todo summaries.
- Scoping/ownership isolation: the server must apply all filtering/sorting/pagination only to todos owned by the authenticated member; the request body does not carry any owner identifier.

Visibility (listMode)
- normal: include only todos not soft-deleted, i.e., multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at IS NULL.
- trash: include only soft-deleted (trashed) todos, i.e., multi_user_todo_todos.deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

Completion (completionStatus)
- all: do not constrain is_complete.
- complete: multi_user_todo_todos.is_complete = true.
- incomplete: multi_user_todo_todos.is_complete = false.

Keyword search (keyword)
- When keyword is a non-empty string, apply text/substring/FTS matching against:
  - multi_user_todo_todos.title
  - multi_user_todo_todos.description (only when description is not null)
- Always scope this search to the authenticated owner.

Date-range filters
- createdFrom/createdTo constrain multi_user_todo_todos.created_at.
  - createdFrom (if non-null): created_at >= createdFrom
  - createdTo (if non-null): created_at <= createdTo
  - If both are provided, validate createdFrom <= createdTo.
- startFrom/startTo constrain multi_user_todo_todos.start_date.
  - Apply bounds only to rows where start_date is non-null; if a bound is present, null start_date rows must not satisfy that bound.
  - If both are provided, validate startFrom <= startTo.
- dueFrom/dueTo constrain multi_user_todo_todos.due_date.
  - Apply bounds only to rows where due_date is non-null; if a bound is present, null due_date rows must not satisfy that bound.
  - If both are provided, validate dueFrom <= dueTo.

Sorting (sortBy + sortDirection)
- sortBy is an allowlist:
  - createdAt -> multi_user_todo_todos.created_at
  - startDate -> multi_user_todo_todos.start_date
  - dueDate -> multi_user_todo_todos.due_date
- sortDirection is interpreted as:
  - For createdAt:
    - newestFirst => created_at DESC
    - oldestFirst => created_at ASC
  - For startDate and dueDate:
    - earliestFirst => ASC
    - latestFirst => DESC
- Reject/validate incompatible combinations so that only the above direction mappings are accepted.

Pagination (page + limit)
- Apply LIMIT/OFFSET after filtering and sorting.
- page is 1-indexed.
- offset = (page - 1) * limit.

Validation
- Validate each from<=to constraint when both bounds are non-null.
- Validate sort keys/directions within the allowlist.

Mapping
- This request DTO maps to query parameters only; it does not directly map to a single todo row/record.

- trashState controls which visibility set to browse using lifecycle/deletion semantics.
  - normal: active (not deleted) todos
  - trash: trashed (soft-deleted) todos

Searching
- If searchText is provided and is non-empty, apply a text/trigram search predicate over multi_user_todo_todos.title and multi_user_todo_todos.description.
- Combine matches so that a todo is returned when it matches on either field (typical OR semantics), while still respecting ownership scope and trash/normal visibility.

Sorting
- sortBy selects the primary ordering column:
  - createdAt => multi_user_todo_todos.created_at
  - startDate => multi_user_todo_todos.start_date (NULLs last)
  - dueDate => multi_user_todo_todos.due_date (NULLs last)
- sortDirection selects the direction:
  - newestFirst/oldestFirst for createdAt (DESC/ASC)
  - earliestFirst/latestFirst for startDate/dueDate (ASC/DESC)
- Apply a deterministic secondary ordering (e.g., by id or created_at) to keep pagination stable.

Pagination
- page is 1-based and together with limit determines offset/limit after filtering/sorting.
- Apply limit and offset exactly as specified after all filters and sorting.

Output mapping (for the operation using this DTO)
- Return paginated todo summaries (IMultiUserTodoTodo.ISummary) containing only the fields required by the summary contract.

results.description:
Per-todo restore outcomes.

Each entry reports whether a specific requested todo was successfully restored from the authenticated member’s trash back to the normal (non-deleted) todo list.

When restoration fails for an entry, errorMessage is returned so the client can explain why that todo was not restored.
results.x-autobe-specification:
Compute results as follows:

1) Determine the set of todo IDs the service will consider.
- The service de-duplicates input todoIds before processing; the considered set is the unique IDs after de-duplication.

2) For each considered todoId, create exactly one result entry.
- success=true if the service restored the todo from trash to normal by clearing deleted_at (set to null) and setting lifecycle_state to the domain’s normal/active lifecycle state.
- success=false if restoration did not occur because the todo was not eligible for restore (commonly due to wrong ownership and/or not currently being in trash per deleted_at and lifecycle_state constraints).

3) errorMessage:
- Include an errorMessage for success=false entries that explains the failure reason in a client-friendly way.

Output invariants:
- results length equals operationSummary.totalRequested.
- Each considered todoId appears exactly once in results.

operationSummary.description:
Aggregated restore counts.

Provides overall metrics for the bulk restore request, including how many todo IDs were processed (after de-duplication) and how many were successfully restored back into the normal todo list.
operationSummary.x-autobe-specification:
Compute operationSummary from results:

- totalRequested: the number of todo IDs considered by the service after de-duplication.
- totalRestored: the count of entries in results where success=true.

Must satisfy:
- operationSummary.totalRequested === results.length
- operationSummary.totalRestored === number of successful items in results

scenario.draft:
Scenario — Member session refresh succeeds and returns a newly issued token pair (token rotation).

1) Call POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/join to register a new member and obtain an initial refresh token R0 (and capture the initial access token A0 if returned).
2) Call POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/refresh with refreshToken = R0.
3) Validate business/security outcomes on the refresh response:
- The response includes a new token pair containing both access and refresh tokens.
- token.refreshable_until and token.expired_at are present and are ISO-8601 date-time strings.
- The response token.refresh is different from R0 (refresh token rotation).
- If A0 was captured, the response token.access is different from A0 (access token rotation).
- The response does not simply echo the input refresh token as the new refresh token.
- If the endpoint also returns profile/authorization data, validate that the returned profile data fields are present (without adding extra assumptions beyond what is returned).
4) Optional security follow-up (still success-path oriented): reuse the old refresh token R0 for another refresh and verify the system behavior is consistent with refresh-rotation expectations (e.g., it should not continue to rotate successfully).

Avoid negative/input-validation assertions; this scenario should focus on successful refresh and token-rotation behavior.

scenario.draft:
Scenario 2 — Refresh replay: after a successful refresh rotates the refresh token, reusing the old refresh token should not succeed.

1) Call POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/join to obtain the initial refresh token R0.
2) Call POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/refresh with refreshToken = R0; capture the rotated refresh token R1 (and the new access/refresh token pair returned on success).
3) Call POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/refresh again with refreshToken = R0 (the previously rotated-away token).
4) Validate failure behavior (business/security assertions):
- The second refresh request must not be treated as a successful refresh.
- The response must not include a newly minted access/refresh token pair in the success token shape.

scenario.draft:
Scenario: Member todo search supports completion filtering, keyword search across title OR description, correct NULL date ordering, and deterministic pagination.

Steps:
1) Register and authenticate as a member via POST /multiUserTodo/auth/member/join.
2) Create multiple normal (non-trash) todos owned by the same authenticated member, with controlled combinations of:
   - Completion state: at least one incomplete and at least one complete.
   - Keyword presence: at least one todo where the keyword appears only in the title, at least one where it appears only in the description, and at least one where it appears in neither field.
   - NULL vs non-NULL dates: at least one todo with start_date = NULL and one with start_date non-NULL; and at least one todo with due_date = NULL and one with due_date non-NULL.
3) Call PATCH /multiUserTodo/member/todos/search to browse normal (non-trash) todos filtered to only incomplete.
   Validate:
   - Every returned todo belongs to the authenticated member.
   - Every returned todo is incomplete.
4) Call PATCH /multiUserTodo/member/todos/search with normal (non-trash) scope, completion filter set to include both states, and enable keyword search for the chosen keyword.
   Validate:
   - Todos returned include the ones whose title or description matches the keyword.
   - Todos returned exclude those where the keyword matches neither title nor description.
5) NULL ordering behavior:
   - Call PATCH /multiUserTodo/member/todos/search with sorting by start_date (one direction) and validate that the API’s documented NULL handling is respected in the returned order.
   - Repeat the same validation for due_date.
6) Pagination determinism:
   - Repeat the exact same search/sort/filter from step 5 but fetch page 2 with a small page size.
   Validate:
   - No overlap of todo IDs between page 1 and page 2.
   - Pagination metadata remains consistent with the same filters/sort.

Business checks: completion filtering applies to normal browsing; keyword search matches across title OR description; returned ordering respects NULL date semantics; pagination is deterministic for identical query inputs.
